body:
You broke the child scene (**SubchildScene**) but didn't completely localize it (didn't clear `SubchildScene`'s `scene_file_path`), so when instantiated, it should instantiate 2 `Sprite2D`s at the same path with the same name, one for the new scene (owner is child) and one for the child scene (original owner). That is, the scene you package contains the original sub-scene.

This should throw an error during adding child while instantiating, but since `_add_child_nocheck()`  is used when instantiating the scene, no error was thrown during instantiation. Adding fails silently.


So, this is not a bug. Normally, two nodes are not allowed to exist on a path. But you change the owner, making this possible. But perhaps a warning should be given.

Good to hear. I didn't know about the scene_file_path property. Seems like a better way to detect if a node is a scene root that what I'm using.

I agree that at least a warning should be given. Packing scenes can be a way to save game progress and it should be easy for users to do it at runtime. Giving them feedback to do it properly is on the right track I think.

I still don't understand why not using unique names seemingly circumvents the issue and why the duplicated node doesn't appear on the remote scene tree.

```
.
Control
Control/MarginContainer
Control/MarginContainer/HBoxContainer
Control/MarginContainer/HBoxContainer/LoadChild1
Control/MarginContainer/HBoxContainer/LoadChild2
Packer
Node2D2                                             # new scene
Node2D2/SubchildScene                               # SubchildScene
Node2D2/SubchildScene/Sprite2D                      # create by instantiating SubchildScene, will be replaced by the one below.  the owner is Node2D2/SubchildScene
Node2D2/SubchildScene/Sprite2D                      # create by instantiating new scene, the owner is Node2D2
```

When instantiating the new scene, SubchildScene will be instantiated first.  Due to the following code, the same path nodes will be replaced. A check should be added here as it may cause leaks.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e1b4101e3460dd9c6ba0b7f8d88e9751b8383f5b/scene/main/node.cpp#L1642

Nodes with unique name enabled will be cached by its **owner**'s `owned_unique_nodes`. The above two nodes are cached by Node2D2/SubchildScene and Node2D2 respectively.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e1b4101e3460dd9c6ba0b7f8d88e9751b8383f5b/scene/main/node.cpp#L2179

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e1b4101e3460dd9c6ba0b7f8d88e9751b8383f5b/scene/main/node.cpp#L1873-L1877

When searching by path, since the script is attached to Node2D2/SubchildScene, the Node2D2/SubchildScene is searched first. If not found, the owner (Node2D2) of the Node2D2/SubchildScene is searched (it is skipped here). In simple terms, there are two nodes with the same unique name in different scenes. Searching from the subscene root will find the one in the subscene first. The special point here is that these two nodes share the same path. In fact, they are not the same path, but each occupies a cache.
Thank you, this explains everything. I guess I should leave the issue open though, since you found a place with potential leaks,
